note: Route types and the options that apply to every type (docs/architecture.md 2.11, decision 6.5). compose(type, options) in packbuilder/routing/route_lib.py and in android/routing/core (PresetSet.compose) turns one type and a set of options into the format-1 preset the planner runs: every request of the type (its one request, or each pool candidate) gets the type's costing_options with each selected option's costing_options merged on top; the fallback request is the same with each option's fallback_costing_options instead; the fallback runs when the request finds no route (every type; the route then carries a warning) and when the route exceeds a fallback_when limit (not for a type with option_fallback_when false). Option names, ranges and defaults checked against docs/docs/api/route/api-reference.md and src/sif/autocost.cc, src/sif/dynamiccost.cc at valhalla tag 3.9.1. Values tuned on trips.json (21 PA/OH trips); see docs/experiments/01-routing.md. The format-1 file is kept as android/routing/testdata/reference/presets-format1.json. Batch D (docs/next-round.md item 13): Shortest is no longer a route type (no type sets option_fallback_when false since then); a stored "shortest" (settings, trip.json) names no type, and the trip takes the default type (Fastest).

checks.note: Valhalla snaps a point to the nearest road within 35 km without saying so (Lake Erie -> 14 km, Binghamton NY on a PA+OH device -> 8 km). The app warns when a route end is further than this from the requested point (route_lib.far_snap_warnings).

every_request.note: Applied by route_lib.request() and the app's ValhallaRequests.route() to every route request of every type and preset (not to the stop-order matrix): costing_options under the preset's own (the preset wins on the same key), stops on every location after the first (the stops and the destination; never the origin, which is the car). Batch C1 (docs/next-round.md item 9, docs/experiments/23-batch-c.md). Option names checked against valhalla tag 3.9.1: src/sif/autocost.cc (alley_factor, default 1), src/sif/dynamiccost.cc and valhalla/sif/dynamiccost.h (alley_penalty 5 s on entering an alley, service_penalty 75 s for auto on entering a generic service road, service_factor default 1), docs/docs/api/route/api-reference.md (search_filter, search_cutoff, preferred_side, street_side_cutoff; the location field street is documented there as not implemented).
every_request.costing_note: alley_factor 5: an alley (service=alley) costs five times its time, so the route uses one only when no ordinary street gets there. Measured on 120 Erie POI pairs with both ends tied (data/r3-run2/c1/probe_through.py): one route used 115 m of alley as a short cut, with alley_factor 5 none did, +5 s in all. alley_factor 10 and service_factor 2 changed nothing more there; generic service roads already carry service_penalty 75 s; driveways, parking aisles and drive-throughs have no auto factor in 3.9.1 and are kept off the ends by the tie below.
every_request.stops_note: Where a stop is tied to the road: the nearest residential-or-higher street within 300 m, never a motorway or a ramp. 1322 Erie POIs with an address tied to the nearest edge as before: 641 to a driveway, 221 to a parking aisle, 63 to an alley, 36 to a service road, 44 to a drive-through, 317 to a street (data/r3-run2/c1/probe_alleys.py). When no such street is within 300 m the engine answers 171 (No suitable edges near location) and the request is asked once more without search_filter and search_cutoff (route_lib.route, RoutePlanner Calls.route): then the place is reached by the service way. A map point (a dropped pin, the app's Stop.tied false, route_lib `_tie` "none") gets none of this: the route goes to the road at the pin. A place whose address names its street is first moved to that street (address_street below). Batch C1 routing fix: a place more than 100 m from any street (inside a large car park) now ends at the street, up to 300 m away; the arrival card then says how far the place still is.
every_request.arrival_side_note: Drive on the right (US). When the chosen route arrives at a stop with the destination on the left (maneuver type 6), the same request is asked once more with preferred_side same and street_side_cutoff tertiary on those stops. Batch D (docs/next-round.md item 16, the owner's answer): on a street of residential class and below (unclassified, residential, service) the engine ignores the side (Valhalla: the side is disabled on an edge of a lower class than the cutoff), so the plain route stays and the place may be on the left; on tertiary and above the side route is kept when it succeeds, arrives at each of those stops on the right (maneuver type 5; type 4, no side, does not count), has no more U-turns than the first, takes at most max_extra_s (60 s) longer and has at most max_extra_maneuvers (2) more guidance instructions (every maneuver but the start and the arrival, as Simpler counts them): one block at most, never a longer loop or a U-turn; else the first route stays. A business on a residential street in Erie, approached along a main road, went around the block (+43 s, +2 instructions) with the C1 rule; now it turns onto its street. A shop on a busy secondary street in Erie keeps the right side (one block, +32 s, +2 instructions). For an alternate a pool picked (Simpler) the side request keeps its alternates and the route the same way as the picked one is the side route (batch D; route_lib.same_way). History: tertiary and above until the C1 routing fix, every street (service_other) in 0.1.4.
every_request.tie_check_note: The ends' check (batch E2, docs/next-round.md item 19; route_lib.decide_ends, RoutePlanner.decide, PlanResult.Ok.tieCheck): the end of each stop is decided once per plan and every route type routes to it (the owner: "The destination point is non-negotiable. The route should end at the same point no matter what route choice."). Its possible ends, best first: a point of interest: its own lot (lot below), its address street (address_street), the nearest street (stops); a place that names its street: that street, the nearest street; any other tied place: the nearest street; and last on every one of these lists the place itself, untied (its own point, no stop tie; batch H, docs/next-round.md, the owner's answers after batch G); a map point: exactly where it is. They are tried in that order with the plan's Fastest request (the driver's options), stop by stop; an end is kept when its route finds a way, takes at most max_extra_s (90 s) longer than the route to the next end on the list with no more U-turns, and its last tail_m (300) metres use none of never_uses (an alley, a drive-through lane; one trace_attributes call on the route's shape, edge_walk, else map_snap; asked only for the end about to be kept); the last end is kept when none before it is. The place itself never wins with an alley or a drive-through lane in its last tail_m metres (C1: no alleys unless there is no other way): its tail is asked when it would win, and when it uses one the nearest street is kept, unless the nearest street finds no way at all. The arrival side is then asked once on the route to the chosen ends; the decided locations (point, tie or no tie, side options) go unchanged into every route type's requests and every re-route. Until 0.1.6 each route type checked its own route (the tie check against the untied request, the lot route against the street end): to a restaurant on Peach Street Simpler's own way into the lot was 94-95 s slower than its own street end, so Simpler ended on Peach Street while Fastest ended in the lot. 450 Erie plans (docs/experiments/26-batch-e2.md): Fastest and Simpler ended at different points in 4, now 0. Batch H (docs/experiments/29-batch-h.md): with the place itself last, Ulta Beauty given as a plain address whose street is out of reach ends at the place again (621.9 s, 32 m, no U-turn; batch E2 kept the nearest street, 586.6 s, 191 m, a U-turn). History: C1 routing fix (the tied route against the same request untied), batch D (also for an alternate a pool picked), batch E (a lot route against its street end). Front doors (docs/next-round.md item 28, 2026-11-21): a lot found around the place's door may be slower than the next end by max_extra_s plus the walk it saves: how much nearer to the door its route ends than the next end's route, at door_walk_m_per_s (1.4 m/s). The lot of a large store is large: to a Walmart Supercenter on Buffalo Road, Erie, from the south-east the way to the lane by the door is 97 s longer than the route to Buffalo Road, which ends 224 m from the door; 211 m of walking saved allow 151 s more, so the route ends by the door. Without a door nothing changes.
every_request.address_street_note: A place whose address names its street (the owner's answer after batch C1; Kotlin Stop.street, route_lib `_street`) is tied to that street when it passes within within_m: valhalla-mobile 0.6.4 has no locate call, so one trace_attributes call (map_snap) matches a grid of point pairs (every probe_step_m within within_m, each pair alone, search_radius probe_radius_m) to their nearest edges; the nearest edge whose name equals the address street (lower case, letters and digits, words through `words`; a road class the stop tie allows) gives the point, end_margin_m inside the edge so it is not a crossing. The location is then that point with the place as display_lat/display_lon (Valhalla takes the side of the street from it); the stop tie still applies. No such street: the place as it is (the nearest residential-or-higher street). Family Dollar, 155 East 12th Street, Erie: East 12th Street (49 m) instead of Holland Street (37 m). 150 Erie places x 3 origins: the route ends on the address street in 411 of 450 plans (236 without), the street found for 146 of 150 places; the probe takes 43 ms (median, PC) (data/r3-run2/c1/fix/measure_street.py).
every_request.entrance_note: The way into a lot (docs/next-round.md item 35; route_lib.decide_entrances, Kotlin RoutePlanner.decideEntrances). The engine picks a way in by its own cost, which counts every small junction of an entrance, so two ways into one lot can be near ties there while one is clearly faster by the clock (the owner's supermarket: 193 s through the signal against 211 s, cost 389 against 374). For a stop that ends in a lot the plan's Fastest route is asked, the place where its last tail_m metres leave the public roads (the first edge whose use is in lot_uses and all after it) is closed with one exclude_polygons square of 2 x box_half_m put into_m along the way inside the lot, and the route is asked again. The other way in is taken, for every route of this plan, when it is at least min_gain_s faster, costs at most within_cost times as much and has no more U-turns; it must have been found with the way in really closed (a request that finds no route is asked once more without any exclusion: that answer does not count) and end within same_end_m of where the first route ends. Measured on 300 plans to large buildings (2026-11-21, the weekly pack's graph): another way in exists for 209, is faster for 40, and 16 plans change with these values (22 s saved in the middle, 34 s at most, the route 180 m shorter in the middle). Every plan decides it again from where the trip is then: a driver who missed the turn is not sent back to it.
every_request.left_out_note: Drive-through lanes and alleys left out of every route (batch E2, docs/next-round.md item 19; route_lib.left_out_rings, Kotlin AddressTie.leftOutRings): the probes a point of interest already gets (address street and lot) also show the edges whose Valhalla use is in uses (drive_through, alley) within within_m of the place; each gets a square of 2 x box_half_m at the middle of its edge, only where that middle is more than clear_m from both ends of the edge and from every other edge the probes see (so the box never touches another edge), nearest first, and every request of the plan carries them as exclude_polygons (at most max_rings rings of 5 vertices: the app's engine allows 100 vertices and 10 km of perimeter). A request that finds no route with them is asked once more without them (route_lib.route, RoutePlanner Calls.route); the ends' check (tie_check.never_uses) then rejects a way in through a lane or an alley, so a lot reached only through a drive-through lane ends on the street: the car wash on West 12th Street, Erie, ends on West 12th Street at the lane's entrance (4.3 min instead of 0.1.6's 4.8 through the wash lane). Left out up front, from the probes, not only after a route touched one: no extra engine call; on 450 Erie plans Fastest is the same route with and without them (450 of 450) and Simpler changes only where its pool reached the lot through an alley (4 routes).
every_request.lot_note: A point of interest ends in its own lot (batch E, docs/next-round.md item 18; route_lib.lot_tie_point, Kotlin AddressTie.lotPoint; a stop that is a business, shop or amenity: Stop.pointOfInterest, route_lib `_poi`). It is probed twice: the address_street probe with edge.use (the filter does not change the match, so the address street point stays the same) and a small probe near it (every probe_step_m within probe_within_m). The nearest edge whose Valhalla use is in uses (driveway, parking_aisle; never alley or drive_through, never another service road) within within_m and at least street_margin_m nearer to the place than every street of the stop tie's classes gives the point, address_street.end_margin_m inside the edge; the location is that point with the place as display_lat/display_lon, no stops options and preferred_side either (Valhalla's default; it marks the stop: no arrival side request there). Batch E2: the lot is the first of the stop's ends; the ends' check (tie_check_note) keeps it when its way in is at most tie_check.max_extra_s slower than the route to the address street end (else the nearest street), with no more U-turns and no alley or drive-through lane in its last 300 m; else the next end. A restaurant on Peach Street, Millcreek: a driveway 20 m away, the side street 45 m, Peach Street 48 m: the route enters from Commons Drive and ends in the lot beside the building (from the north and from the south). Without the 10 m street margin 25 of 38 downtown Erie sample places found some driveway nearer than their street, with it 13. The small probe: with the 50 m grid alone the pair at that restaurant matched a driveway 20.5 m away reached from Mandy Lane instead of the one 20.0 m away reached from Commons Drive. 450 Erie plans (150 places x 3 origins; docs/experiments/25-batch-e.md): 227 end in a lot (76 places), 7 go back to the street end by the tie check, the other 216 are unchanged; no more U-turns, no alley; PC planning median 66 -> 83 ms. Front doors (docs/next-round.md item 28, 2026-11-21): for a point of interest that is a large building the search pack gives the point where customers go in (its poi_door table: a mapped entrance, else for a shop the side its parking is on; packbuilder/search/doors.py; route_lib `_door`, Kotlin Stop.door), and the lot is looked for around that door (the small probe and every distance are the door's) with door_uses: a plain service road counts too, because the lane along a store's front is often mapped as one, and by the door it is not the delivery road behind the building. The centroid of a large store is the middle of its roof, 60 m or more from every lane, so the nearest lane was as often the one behind it: a Walmart Supercenter in Erie ended on the service road at the back, 121 m from its door, now at the lane by the door (7 m). 300 large buildings of Pennsylvania x 2 origins (docs/experiments/33-front-doors.md): the route ends within 30 m of the door in 92 % of the plans to a shop whose front is known from its parking (38 % before), median 11 m (39 m); with a mapped main entrance 94 % (32 %).

route_types.label: Fastest
route_types.tuning: Valhalla defaults (maneuver_penalty 5 s, use_highways 0.5, use_tolls 0.5, use_distance 0, top_speed 140 km/h).

route_types.label: Simpler
route_types.tuning: maneuver_penalty alone is noise for this goal (60 s: mean -0.5 maneuvers but +1.5% time; 120-300 s: more time, maneuvers not reduced). Pool of Fastest + 2 alternates + two maneuver_penalty routes, pick the fewest maneuvers within +5% time: 6/21 trips change, never more maneuvers than Fastest, about 3 route calls per request.
route_types.batch_d: The owner's answers (docs/next-round.md item 13, 2026-11-18): a Simpler route may take up to 10 % (max_time_increase) and never more than 10 minutes (max_time_extra_s 600) longer than the quickest route of its pool; turns are every guidance instruction (min_maneuvers, as before). A wider window alone took I-79, I-80 and PA 8 to a road north of Butler because the pool never held the exit 99 / US 422 route; the fourth candidate (use_highways 1.0 with maneuver_penalty 60) keeps to major roads and brings that route in. Measured on the 21 reference trips and 60 Erie-region trips (data/r3-run2/d/measure_pool.py; docs/experiments/24-batch-d.md): with the old three candidates and the new window 31 of 60 Erie trips differ from Fastest; with the fourth 35, 66 instructions fewer in all, +2.6 min on average where it differs; on the 21 reference trips 7 differ, +1.8 min on average (+2.4 without it). maneuver_penalty 120, use_highways 1.0 alone, a candidate that also avoids living streets, tracks and service roads, more alternates (4) and alternates on a second candidate added no more than the fourth candidate at one more call each, or nothing.

route_types.label: Eco
route_types.tuning: Proxy only (Valhalla has no fuel model): equal weight on distance and time. 9/21 trips differ, mean -3.7% distance, +0.4% time. top_speed below 113 km/h made routes leave 70 mph interstates entirely (+7..16% time) and was rejected. A candidate pool with min_distance within +5% time gave about the same result (-3.9% / +0.2%) at 3x the cost.
route_types.format_2: offered false: the route sheet never shows Eco; the planner and the tests still run it (docs/architecture.md 2.11 rule 5).

options.label: Avoid highways
options.tuning: exclude_highways (hard exclusion of motorway-class roads; needs service_limits.allow_hard_exclusions) gave 0 motorway km at +25.5% time. use_highways=0 also penalises trunk roads 4x: 24 km of motorway left, +45% time. In 3.9.1 the exclusion only forbids driving ONTO a motorway (dynamiccost.h CheckExclusions), so when the trip starts on one it may stay on motorways all the way (I-90 near the OH line -> Erie: 46.7 of 48.3 km on I-90/I-79). So the fallback runs both when the exclusion finds no route and when the result still has more than 0.5 motorway km; the route with fewer motorway km wins (same trip: 1.9 km to the next exit).

options.label: Avoid tolls
options.tuning: use_tolls=0 (toll edges cost about 5x) removed every toll km on the 4 trips that had tolls (PA Turnpike, Ohio Turnpike); exclude_tolls and an extra toll_booth_penalty gave the same routes. Soft option kept: it cannot fail. Limitation: a trip that starts ON the Turnpike keeps the Fastest route (I-76 near the OH line -> Pittsburgh: 42.9 toll km either way); exclude_tolls cannot help there because it also allows staying on a toll road.
options.format_2: Now the hard exclude_tolls for every type: Valhalla ignores the soft use_tolls when shortest is set, so the soft form left Shortest with tolls (review finding F2: Carlisle to King of Prussia, Shortest with use_tolls 0: 167.5 km with tolls; with exclude_tolls 168.6 km without). A stop or destination on a toll road cannot be reached under the exclusion (No path could be found), so use_tolls 0 is the fallback when the request finds no route, and the route then says so (docs/architecture.md 2.11, owner question 5 of 6.38). No fallback_when: a trip that starts on a toll road may stay on it (the owner accepted this on 2026-11-15).
